newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends up on adjustment, Tokyo's rise.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends up on adjustment, Tokyo's rise.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed higher on a technical adjustment after recent falls, but trading remained lacklustre in the absence of fresh consumer demand, dealers said.
They said a firmer Tokyo market helped local prices.
"There's some adjustment in prices but there's no real buyers in the market," said one local dealer. "Prices should maintain at current levels."
Dealers said downside is likely to be limited on expectations of lower production in February due to fewer working days during the month and the onset of wintering.
The market is closed from February 6 to 11 for the twin festivals of Chinese New Year and Eid al-Fitr.
At the close, benchmark March RSS1 buyer was quoted by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board at 300 cents ($1.20) a kg, up a cent from Monday.
March SMR 20 buyer was also up a cent to 295 ($1.18) a kg.
Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 293 cents a kg, SMR CV at 356, SMR L at 336, SMR 5 at 302, SMR 10 at 294 and drum latex FOB at 233-234.
